Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with 6 years of experience in analytics and data science, including 4+ years as a data scientist. Experienced in building forecasting and churn models used by operations and retention teams, designing experiments, and maintaining analytics data models. Strong Python, SQL and statistical skills, with a focus on translating business questions into actionable analyses. Moving towards machine learning engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels), SQL (BigQuery), R (tidyverse, brms), dbt
Machine learning and statistics: Forecasting, customer analytics, A/B testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics
Tools: Git, Jupyter, Looker

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox, meal-kit subscriptions | Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
- Built a weekly demand forecasting model for individual recipes using LightGBM and calendar features. Used by operations to order ingredients, the model reduced forecast error (WAPE) from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%.
- Built an XGBoost churn propensity model used to target retention offers; validated uplift using a holdout.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; built the team's sequential testing calculator.
- Present results to leadership monthly.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Conducted customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports using R Markdown.

EDUCATION

MSc Statistics, Distinction | University of the Lothians | 2020
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019

LANGUAGES
English (native), Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It uses strong quantified outcomes, especially the reduction in WAPE from 23% to 14% and estimated 9% reduction in food waste. The experience bullets demonstrate business impact, statistical ability, experimentation, Python/SQL capability, and exposure to production analytics work. The main content limitation is that it presents the candidate primarily as a data scientist rather than as a machine learning engineer building and operating production systems. Several bullets also describe activities without clarifying the technical delivery lifecycle, such as deployment, monitoring, testing, or operational ownership; these should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard chronology, and searchable keywords such as Python, SQL, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, BigQuery, dbt, Git, forecasting, and A/B testing. There are no apparent tables, graphics, headers/footers, or unusual formatting that would impair parsing. However, the AI screening probability for this particular role is low to moderate because several high-priority terms from the advert are absent: machine learning engineer, AI systems, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, GCP, MLOps, orchestration, data ingestion pipelines, language models, chat assistants, and RAG. BigQuery provides evidence connected to Google Cloud, but the CV does not explicitly identify it as GCP. Only add or clarify terms that accurately reflect the candidate's real work; do not add unsupported tools or capabilities.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate aligns well with the quantitative and applied modelling aspects of the role. They have a relevant quantitative education, strong Python, production SQL, dbt analytics modelling, forecasting, churn modelling, feature use through calendar variables, experimentation, and experience presenting results to stakeholders. The forecasting and churn models have clear operational or commercial use. The CV does not establish at least four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; it establishes four-plus years as a data scientist, with production-use models but no explicit model-serving or ML engineering ownership. The candidate material also does not show AI products such as chat assistants or RAG, software engineering capabilities involving model serving, monitoring, or data versioning, MLOps/orchestration tools, or data ingestion pipelines. The listed degrees are Statistics and Mathematics rather than machine learning, computer science, or an engineering degree, so the specific degree requirement is not clearly met. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting. The CV does show strong Python and related applied ML experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CV CHANGES:
1. In the Technical Skills section, change the BigQuery entry from "SQL (BigQuery)" to "SQL; BigQuery (Google Cloud)" if the candidate used BigQuery as a Google Cloud service. This makes the existing cloud experience searchable as GCP without claiming experience with another cloud platform.

2. In the Data Scientist section under Thistlebox, revise the forecasting bullet to make the supported feature-engineering experience explicit. For example: "Built a weekly demand forecasting model for individual recipes using LightGBM; performed feature engineering with calendar features. Used by operations to order ingredients, reducing WAPE from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%." Do not describe this as a data ingestion pipeline, model serving, or MLOps work unless those activities are documented in the candidate's actual experience.

3. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence "Moving towards machine learning engineering." with a more evidence-based description of the current profile, such as: "Experienced in developing applied machine learning models for operational and retention use cases, with production SQL and analytics data-modelling experience." This positions the candidate more strongly for the role without claiming four years as a machine learning engineer or unsupported production engineering experience.

4. In the Technical Skills section, consider separating the existing skills into ATS-clear categories with explicit supported terminology: "Programming: Python, R, SQL"; "Machine Learning: scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, forecasting, customer analytics, feature engineering with calendar features"; "Statistics: A/B testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics, statsmodels"; "Data and Analytics Engineering: BigQuery (Google Cloud), dbt"; and "Tools: Git, Jupyter, Looker." Only use "feature engineering" in this form because the CV documents the use of calendar features.

MINOR CV ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise "Built an XGBoost churn propensity model used to target retention offers; validated uplift using a holdout." to "Built an XGBoost churn propensity model used to target retention offers; evaluated targeting uplift using a holdout set." This is slightly clearer technically while remaining faithful to the original information.

6. In the Thistlebox section, retain the production SQL and dbt bullet but make its scope more explicit without overstating it: "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer." This is already strong evidence and should remain prominent because it supports the role's data-pipeline and production-data requirements, although it does not by itself demonstrate ML serving or MLOps.

At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)

requirements.requirement: Familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured and easy to scan. It uses quantified achievements effectively, including the reduction in WAPE from 23% to 14% and the estimated 9% reduction in food waste. The experience bullets show relevant modelling, experimentation, SQL and analytics engineering work rather than listing responsibilities alone. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role positioning: the document presents strong data-science experience, while the target role requires machine-learning engineering, production software engineering and AI-product experience. The CV does not establish model deployment, serving, monitoring, data versioning or end-to-end production operation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, consistent dates, conventional job titles and searchable technology names such as Python, BigQuery, dbt, LightGBM, XGBoost and Git. Keyword coverage is good for data science and cloud analytics, but weak for this specific vacancy. The CV does not contain supported evidence for model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLOps, orchestration, AI assistants, RAG, language models, text datasets, CI/CD, automated tests or data ingestion pipelines. Consequently, its AI-screening probability for this particular Machine Learning Engineer role is low-to-moderate despite strong general data-science ATS compatibility. Do not add those terms unless the candidate can substantiate them.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python, Google Cloud, feature engineering, statistical modelling, experimentation, customer analytics and production SQL/dbt work. The forecasting and churn models are relevant applied machine-learning examples, and the quantified operational and retention outcomes are valuable for a customer-operations context. However, the candidate's material shows significant gaps against several must-have requirements: the degree is in Statistics and Mathematics rather than machine learning, computer science or engineering; the experience is as a Data Scientist rather than four years as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production; there is no evidence of AI products such as chat assistants or RAG; no evidence of model serving, monitoring or data versioning; and no evidence of MLOps or orchestration tools. Data ingestion pipelines are also not demonstrated. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be solved through wording alone. The document does show a relevant quantitative foundation, strong Python, cloud analytics experience and production-facing modelling/data work.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the production scope more precise without implying unsupported ML deployment. For example, change the final sentence to: "Experienced in applied machine learning for operational and retention use cases, with production SQL in BigQuery and dbt analytics-layer modelling." This keeps the strongest supported production keywords while avoiding an implied claim of production model serving.

2. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Data and analytics engineering" to "Data and Analytics Engineering" and keep the supported tools together as: "BigQuery (Google Cloud), dbt, production SQL." This improves ATS matching for cloud and production-data work without claiming unsupported data ingestion or MLOps experience.

3. In the Data Scientist role at Thistlebox, revise the forecasting bullet so the model-building, feature-engineering and operational-use keywords appear earlier: "Built and evaluated a weekly LightGBM demand-forecasting model for individual recipes, using calendar-feature engineering; adopted by operations for ingredient ordering, reducing WAPE from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%." Do not add deployment, serving or monitoring language, because it is not supported by the original candidate information.

4. In the Data Scientist role at Thistlebox, revise the churn bullet to make the evaluation method and business use more ATS-readable: "Built an XGBoost churn-propensity model for retention-offer targeting and evaluated targeting uplift with a holdout set." This is a minor clarity enhancement using only existing evidence.

5. In the Professional Experience section, change "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer" to the past/present-tense-consistent wording "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models in the analytics layer." This is clearer and preserves the strongest truthful cloud and analytics-engineering evidence.

6. In the Technical Skills section, keep "feature engineering" as a standalone searchable skill rather than only embedding it in "feature engineering with calendar features." Use: "Machine learning: scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, forecasting, feature engineering, customer analytics." The calendar-feature example remains in the experience bullet as evidence.
